item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 251131
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM EDT Fri Sep 25 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Gonzalo, located about 160 miles east-southeast of the
southernmost Cabo Verde Islands, and on Tropical Storm Fay, located
well to the west-southwest of the Azores.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&

Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Gonzalo are issued under WMO
header WTNT32 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT2.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Gonzalo are issued under WMO
header WTNT22 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMAT2.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Brown

...FAY SLIGHTLY STRONGER..
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM GMT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...30.1N 42.5W
ABOUT 1040 MI...1670 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM GMT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was
located near latitude 30.1 North, longitude 42.5 West. Fay is moving
toward the west near 3 mph (6 km/h).  A gradual turn to the
west-southwest then southwest at a slower forward speed is expected
over the next few of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 60 mph (95 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Some slight strengthening is possible over the 
next few hours.  Gradual weakening, however, is still expected 
through the weekend.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Roberts

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Forecast Discussion Number 22
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM GMT Fri Sep 25 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 251437
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Storm Fay Discussion Number  22
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 PM GMT Fri Sep 25 2026
 
Convection continues to increase mostly on the northern side of 
Fay, while resisting dry air entrainment based as displayed on the 
visible and water vapor imagery. The lastest TAFB Dvorak fix came in 
at T2.5/45 kt, however a recent SAR pass found peak winds around 55 
kt. In addition, the objective intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS are 
in the range of 37-42 kt. A recent ASCAT pass showed that some of 
the peak wind vectors were around 40 kt, but given the small size 
of Fay, it is possible that the ASCAT is undersampling the peak 
winds. Based on a compromise of all the available data, the initial 
intensity is raised to 50 kt for this advisory. 
 
Additional strengthening is still possible over the next several 
hours, as Fay is in a region of weak deep-layer shear and 
marginally favorable thermodynamic conditions. The statistical 
GFS/ECMWF SHIPS intensity guidance indicates that northerly wind 
shear will increase tonight, which should help force dry air 
into the cyclone. Therefore, Fay should gradually weaken through 
the period, and degenerate into a post-tropical cyclone during the 
weekend. The current NHC intensity forecast is in good agreement 
with the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids.
 
Fay's initial motion is estimated to be due west, or 275/3 kt and is 
steered by a subtropical ridge anchored over the central Atlantic. 
The initial position for Fay has been adjusted to the left of the 
previous advisory and the center of the cyclone appears to have 
reformed to the northeast.  By Saturday, a gradual turn toward the 
west-southwest and southwest is forecast while Fay weakens and 
become a vertically shallow remnant low steered by the low-level 
flow. The latest NHC track forecast is similar to the previous one 
and lies close to the GDMI ensemble mean and the HCCA corrected 
consensus aid.

item.title: Tropical Storm Gonzalo Public Advisory Number 2a
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM CVT Fri Sep 25 2026 
000
WTNT32 KNHC 251157
TCPAT2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Gonzalo Intermediate Advisory Number 2A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL072026
1100 AM CVT Fri Sep 25 2026
 
...GONZALO STRENGTHENS AS GUSTY WINDS SPREAD ACROSS THE CABO VERDE 
ISLANDS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM CVT...1200 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.7N 22.6W
ABOUT 120 MI...195 KM E OF THE SOUTHERNMOST CABO VERDE ISLANDS
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 340 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* The Cabo Verde Islands
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this case within 12
hours.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM CVT (1200 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Gonzalo was 
located near latitude 14.7 North, longitude 22.6 West. Gonzalo is 
moving toward the north-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h). This motion 
is expected to continue over the next several days, with a slower 
forward speed this weekend. On the forecast track, the center will 
pass near or over portions of the Cabo Verde Islands today and 
tonight.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 50 mph (85 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Small intensity fluctuations are possible today, with 
a gradual weakening trend forecast to begin this weekend.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 175 miles (280 km) 
from the center. Sal International Airport recently reported a wind 
gust of 41 mph (66 km/h).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Gonzalo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDAT2 and WMO header WTNT42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are spreading over the Cabo Verde
Islands and will continue through the day.
 
RAINFALL: Tropical Storm Gonzalo is expected to produce rainfall
totals of 1 to 3 inches (25 to 75 mm) across the eastern portions of
the Cabo Verde Islands today and on Saturday with less than 1 inch
anticipated for the western side of the island chain. Heavy rain
along the coastal areas of Guinea-Bissau, The Gambia, and Senegal
will produce totals between 2 to 4 inches (50 to 100 mm) with
isolated higher amounts along the immediate coast.
 
SURF: Swells generated by the storm are expected to affect the Cabo
Verde Islands through Saturday. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM CVT.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Gonzalo Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM CVT Fri Sep 25 2026 
958 
WTNT42 KNHC 250842
TCDAT2
 
Tropical Storm Gonzalo Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL072026
800 AM CVT Fri Sep 25 2026
 
Gonzalo remains an asymmetric tropical storm, with wind shear 
displacing the deep convection over the eastern and southern 
portions of the center. Satellite intensity estimates from TAFB and 
UW-CIMSS are around 35-40 kt. Given the earlier scatterometer data 
depicting 40 kt and a steady satellite appearance, the initial 
intensity for this advisory is held at 40 kt.
 
The initial motion remains north-northwestward at 340/8 kt. The 
storm is expected to continue moving north-northwestward during the 
next couple of days, steered by the flow of a deep mid-level trough 
over the eastern Atlantic. As the trough lifts northwestward later 
in the forecast period, the steering currents will become very weak, 
and Gonzalo is forecast to slow down and meander over the eastern 
Atlantic. On the forecast track, the center will pass near or over 
portions of the Cabo Verde Islands today and tonight. The official 
NHC track forecast is lies between the HCCA corrected consensus and 
GDMI aids.
 
Gonzalo has about 12 to 18 hours within a marginally conducive 
environment for some strengthening, with sea surface temperatures 
near 27-28 deg C. After that time, vertical wind shear is forecast 
to increase, becoming fairly strong by day 2. Along the forecast 
track, sea surface temperatures will also cool, and mid-level 
relative humidity values will begin to drop into the 50, and then 
40 percent range. The NHC intensity forecast is similar to the 
previous advisory. Global model-simulated infrared satellite imagery 
depicts Gonzalo becoming devoid of deep convection in about 2 to 3 
days. Thus, the forecast shows the system becoming a post-tropical 
remnant low at that time, and it is expected to remain a remnant low 
through day 5.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Tropical storm conditions are expected to spread across portions
of the Cabo Verde Islands, where a Tropical Storm Warning is in
effect, today and will continue through tonight.
 
2. Heavy rains from Gonzalo could affect the eastern islands of Cabo
Verde and the western coast of Africa between Guinea-Bissau to
Senegal today through Saturday. Areas of flash flooding will be
possible along the western coast of Africa with some isolated flash
flood concerns for the eastern islands of Cabo Verde.
